gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-inria-sans: Inria Sans moves like bent copper pipe, tubular and easy to see through. Cherry Swash can go big up top, its horseshoe-wide c on show, while this sans stays modest below.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-istok-web: This body text reads rounded and approachable, each letter leaving one side clearly open. Istok Web sits beneath Cherry Swash, whose heavy diagonals and horseshoe-wide c give the page its commanding top line.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-jost: Horseshoe curves, then clean lines: Cherry Swash opens its c wide, and Jost leaves broad gaps at its terminals. Loud on top, quiet underneath, and the sans never competes with the heading.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-jura: Commanding from the first letter, Cherry Swash bends its c open like a horseshoe. Jura holds its strokes as constant as bent wire, and Cherry Swash earns its keep when big and short.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-k2d: Cherry Swash opens its c like a horseshoe and gives every diagonal the heft of a vertical. And K2D, tube-thick through every bend, would carry paragraphs with a steady, clean texture.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-kanchenjunga: Cherry Swash opens its c like a horseshoe and weights its diagonals like its verticals, built to stand out. Kanchenjunga stays crisp at low resolution, a drafting-pen line that never clogs.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-kantumruy-pro: Smooth and hairline-free, this sans has an e whose eye opens clearly to the right. Kantumruy Pro would carry paragraphs without fuss under Cherry Swash, whose horseshoe-wide c does the commanding.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-kodchasan: Clean and open, Kodchasan has terminals that hang free and no calligraphic thinning. Beneath Cherry Swash's horseshoe c and heavy diagonals, that restraint is the pair's best trait: one voice loud, one steady.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-koho: That horseshoe-wide c, drawn with a constant stroke, is Cherry Swash's calling card. KoHo's wide apertures would keep pages of text moving smoothly, with a clean, steady texture all the way down.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-kosugi: Kosugi bends like wire, its c jawed open like pliers. Cherry Swash's commanding horseshoe c sits over that wire-bent sans-serif, and the heft-against-wire difference is what stands out.
